newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 21.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAY THE TUBE BLEW A FUSE
Last night a complete power failure left the underground system paralysed for up to one and a half hours with 276 trains stranded, containing 20,000 tube passengers.
YEN HOLDS TIGHT IN JAPAN BANK CRISIS
The yen held out against an expected switch to the dollar in last night's Asian trading, despite the shutdown of Japanese regional bank Hanwa because of bad real estate-related loans.
National Australia Bank's British and Irish assets have made smaller contributions than in 1995 and 1994 to record profits of 2.1 billion Australian dollars, or one billion stg.
DEPOSITORS IN HANWA KEEP THEIR COOL

Despite the Japanese Ministry of Finance's closure of Hanwa Bank, the first of a commercial bank in the postwar period, depositors in the bank reacted calmly on the whole. The finance ministry's move is being seen as welcome progress towards a clean-up of the Japanese financial system.
LIBERTY SETS ITS SIGHTS ON THE NERVOUS MONEY

In response to uncertainty on world financial markets, Liberty International has launched two Jersey based money funds to invest solely in liquid short-term financial instruments. The funds have been rated AAA by Standard & Poor's and will be listed on the Dublin stock exchange.
